'''Prasad V. Tetali''' is an Indian-American mathematician and computer scientist who works as a professor at [[Carnegie Mellon University]]. His research concerns [[probability theory]], [[discrete mathematics]], and [[approximation algorithm]]s.

Tetali was born in [[Visakhapatnam]], [[India]] but is now a United States citizen. He graduated from [[Andhra University]] in 1984, earned a master's degree in computer science in 1986 from the [[Indian Institute of Science]],<ref name="cv">[http://people.math.gatech.edu/~tetali/PUBLIS/Tetali.CV.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2015-01-14.</ref> and completed his doctorate in 1991 at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] of [[New York University]] under the supervision of [[Joel Spencer]].<ref name="cv"/><ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=58678}}</ref> After postdoctoral studies, he joined the School of Mathematics at Georgia Tech in 1994, and added a joint appointment in computing in 2001.<ref name="cv"/>  At Georgia Tech, his doctoral students have included [[Adam Marcus (mathematician)|Adam Marcus]].<ref name="mg"/> He was editor-in-chief of ''[[SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics]]'' from 2009 to 2011.<ref name="cv"/> He moved to Carnegie Mellon University in 2021 to become the head of the Department of Mathematical Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |last=University |first=Carnegie Mellon |title=Prasad Tetali - Mathematical Sciences - Mellon College of Science - Carnegie Mellon University |url=https://www.cmu.edu/math/people/faculty/tetali.html |access-date=2023-11-08 |website=www.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref>

Tetali became a [[fellow]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2009,<ref name="cv"/> and one of the inaugural fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012.<ref name="cv"/><ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-01-14.</ref>
